Iron Mountain.why: Data center developer/operator leasing hyperscale and enterprise capacity (Northern Virginia, Richmond, London, Amsterdam, Mumbai) for AI inference build-outs; Global Data Center revenue +39% YoY, plus hyperscale data center decommissioning.
Iron Mountain.evidence: Iron Mountain Q2 FY2026 (08-05-2026), CEO Will Meaney: 'We signed a 25-megawatt lease in July, fully leasing our London 3 asset... Both of these leases are a direct result of the large and expanding pipeline we have around AI inference. Also in July, a major global hyperscaler leased 51 megawatts in Mumbai as part of a 10-year contract.'

players.product: Data center leasing to hyperscalers and enterprises (Northern Virginia, Richmond, London, Amsterdam, Mumbai; ~325 MW of leasable capacity energizing over the next 24 months) plus hyperscale and neocloud data center decommissioning

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2: revenue of $2.03 billion, up 19% reported and 17% organic (about $65 million above the company's projection, mainly from ALM hyperscale decommissioning); adjusted EBITDA $727 million, up 16%; AFFO $433 million, up 17% ($1.44 per share). Data center, ALM and digital businesses together grew more than 50% and were 35% of Q2 revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $2.03 billion (+19%); adj EBITDA $727 million (+16%); AFFO $433 million (+17%)

quarterly_data.signal: Raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue $7.94 billion-$8.01 billion (16% growth at midpoint), adjusted EBITDA $2.945 billion-$2.975 billion (15%), AFFO $1.76 billion-$1.78 billion or $5.87-$5.93 per share. Q3 2026 outlook: revenue approximately $1.98 billion and adjusted EBITDA approximately $745 million, both up 13%, AFFO approximately $440 million ($1.47 per share). ALM full-year revenue now expected to approach $1 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue $7.94 billion-$8.01 billion; adj EBITDA $2.945 billion-$2.975 billion; Q3 revenue ~$1.98 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Global Data Center revenue of $263 million in Q2, up $73 million or 39% YoY, driven by lease commencements and positive pricing; data center adjusted EBITDA $137 million (52.2% margin, up 140 bp). Q2: signed 13 MW of new leases (including 10 MW in Amsterdam), commenced 25 MW, renewed 189 leases totaling 4 MW at cash/GAAP renewal spreads of 12% and 14%.
quarterly_data.figure: data center revenue $263 million (+39%); 52.2% margin; 13 MW signed; 25 MW commenced

quarterly_data.signal: Data center leasing: 13 MW leased in Q2 and another 75 MW in July, bringing year-to-date leasing to 110 MW versus the original 100 MW full-year target, which CEO expects to 'meaningfully exceed'. July wins: a 25 MW lease fully leasing the London 3 asset and a 10 MW Amsterdam lease, both attributed to the 'large and expanding pipeline we have around AI inference'; a major global hyperscaler leased 51 MW in Mumbai on a 10-year contract, with another 100 MW of future development capacity in India.
quarterly_data.figure: 110 MW leased YTD; 25 MW London 3; 51 MW Mumbai (10-year)

quarterly_data.signal: Approximately 325 MW of leasable capacity expected to energize over the next 24 months (down from 400 MW last call after the leasing), with pipeline across Richmond, Europe and India and further capacity after that period largely in Northern Virginia; CEO: much of the pipeline is 'building out of inference capacity for the hyperscale community'. Q2 growth capex was $553 million.
quarterly_data.figure: ~325 MW energizing over 24 months; growth capex $553 million

quarterly_data.signal: Asset Lifecycle Management (ALM) revenue of $288 million, up 88% (82% organic); data center decommissioning revenue increased more than 100% YoY, helped by $30 million of timing benefit from large hyperscaler projects accelerated into the quarter; memory prices remain elevated versus last year. A neocloud customer in Europe selected Iron Mountain to decommission and remarket tens of thousands of IT assets. CFO: the hyperscale data center decommissioning TAM is expected to double from $3 billion to about $6 billion over the next four or five years, and future refresh will be more GPU-based gear; enterprise ALM revenue a little over $600 million this year. Acquired Group ATF (France, Belgium), closed around August 1st.
quarterly_data.figure: ALM revenue $288 million (+88%); decommissioning TAM $3 billion to $6 billion
